Hydrophytes live in freshwater or wet soil and absorb water through their whole surface. Xerophytes live in very dry environments and reduce water loss with adaptations such as deep roots, few stomata and a thick waxy cuticle.
Many hydrophytes lose excess water through stomata on floating leaves. Halophytes store excess salts in cells or excrete them through salt glands on leaves.

Hydrophytes absorb water through their whole surface and remove excess water through stomata on floating leaves. Xerophytes obtain water with deep roots and reduce water loss with few stomata and a thick waxy cuticle; some store water in succulent organs. Halophytes absorb salts to make their bodies hypertonic, helping prevent water from moving out of their cells; they may store or excrete excess salt.
